title: Cycle buffer & staff-flex policy rollout: proactive capacity planning for Q2
creator: Leah Morgan
description:
Problem: Our current cycle planning process leaves teams exposed to last-minute scope cuts, uneven staffing across high-priority initiatives, and frequent spillover. This creates churn for platform teams (serving/runtime, console) and delays delivery on OKRs that are customer-facing.

Proposal: Introduce a formal 'Cycle Buffer & Staff-Flex' policy for the upcoming Q2 planning cycle. Key components: (1) 8% cross-team buffer of engineering capacity reserved for unplanned high-priority incidents or rollups, (2) a lightweight staff-flex roster to temporarily reassign 1-2 engineers for up to 4 weeks between related initiatives, (3) an explicit scope-cut ladder (triage rules) that PMs follow during commitments, and (4) a pre-approved list of low-cost de-scoped items (10–20% per epic) that can be dropped without re-architecting.

Why this helps: Provides predictable room to absorb unplanned work, reduces last-minute scope cutting, improves on-time OKR delivery, and reduces context-switching overhead by making reassignments explicit and time-boxed.

Trade-offs considered: Larger buffers mean slower feature throughput but fewer regressions; smaller buffers increase risk of scope spill. Staff-flex reduces deep specialization availability and may impact velocity if overused. The recommended 8%/1-2 headcount cap is a conservative starting point; we'll iterate based on Q2 retrospective metrics.

Deliverables: (A) Policy doc + decision matrix for scope-cut ladder, (B) Roster + ops runbook for staff-flex handoffs, (C) Updated cycle planning template for PMs & ENG leads, (D) Dashboard widgets in Console showing buffer utilization and reassignment churn.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc published in Confluence with sign-off from Eng, Design and GtM leads
Roster template and on-call style handoff checklist available and tested in one pilot team
Cycle planning template updated and used by 4 pilot tribes for Q2 commitments
Buffer utilization metric implemented on Console dashboard and shows recorded allocations for pilot teams
